To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the energy consumption of an 802.11 network interface is linearly proportional to the number of packets transmitted, received or dropped, and that the energy consumption per packet is linearly proportional (with a small constant offset) to the size of the packet, for both unicast and broadcast transmissions.

the power consumption of a wireless network interface in an ad hoc environment depends on the following: 1) the number of packets sent, received and discarded, 2) the size of each packet, 3) the number of packet collisions, 4) the number of times that the interface has to retransmit each packet and 5) the amount of idle time.
• Sending and receiving a 1024 byte data packet consumes 2.4 J of energy and discarding a 1024-byte data packet consumes 0.8 J of energy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the energy consumption of wireless interfaces in ad hoc networks.
the design and evaluation of energy-aware network protocols.
the development of energy-aware protocols for wireless ad hoc networks.

a wireless network interface consumes more energy when transmitting data than when receiving data.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is possible to measure energy consumption for a wireless network interface in a way that is useful to protocol developers.
we have obtained detailed measurements for the energy consumption behavior for a widely used IEEE 802.1 1 wireless network interface operating under realistic conditions.
the energy consumption of an IEEE 802. 11 wireless network interface can be modeled as a collection of simple linear equations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy consumption of an 802.11 interface is dominated by the time spent in the idle state and that the energy consumed per bit transmitted is very small compared to the idle time.
energy consumption of a wireless network interface can be accurately predicted using a small number of simple linear equations, even in an ad hoc network.
